name: Web-Stat – Live Visitor Analytics
author: Web-Stat

sections.description:
Web-Stat is a website analytics and visitor tracking service for WordPress. See visits as they happen: recent visitors, their entrance pages, where they came from and whether they have visited before. Explore traffic with live reports, referrer statistics and a visitor map. Plus adds navigation and click-path reports.

Install and activate the plugin to set up tracking. Open Web-Stat from your WordPress admin menu to view your stats. You can also access your reports on the Web-Stat website. Explore the live demo.

What you can see

  • Live visitors: See recent visits as they arrive, including entrance pages, referrers, device details and approximate location.
  • Traffic sources: Find visits from search engines, social media, other websites and direct traffic.
  • Returning visitors: See which visitors have been to your site before.
  • Navigation and click-paths (Plus): Follow the pages visitors view within your site and analyze their journeys.
  • Website statistics: Review visits over time, entrance pages, referrers and visitor locations.
  • Advanced reporting: Paid plans add longer history, deeper engagement reports, conversions, custom events and downtime monitoring, depending on the plan.

Free and paid plans

The free plan includes up to 5,000 page views per month, the latest 50 visits and one month of report history. If your site reaches its monthly page-view limit, tracking pauses until the next month or until you increase capacity.

Paid plans increase capacity and add features:

  • Basic: $4.95/month or $49.50/year; up to 10,000 page views per month and six months of report history.
  • Plus: $9.95/month or $99.50/year; up to 100,000 page views per month and 12 months of history, with navigation and click-path reports, time-on-site and bounce rates.
  • Pro: $19.95/month or $199.50/year; up to 300,000 page views per month and 24 months of history, with conversions, custom events and downtime monitoring.
  • Max: $49.95/month or $499.50/year; up to 500,000 page views per month and 60 months of history.

Prices are in USD. See the full plan comparison for current prices, limits and the features included with each plan.

Hosted analytics and privacy

Web-Stat is a hosted analytics service provided by Web Tracking Services, LLC. The plugin connects your WordPress site to Web-Stat; analytics data is processed on Web-Stat’s servers, not stored solely in your WordPress database. A Web-Stat account is required and is set up when you install the plugin.

The tracking code sends visit information to Web-Stat, including page URLs, referrers, IP addresses and browser/device details. Location is estimated from IP addresses. Optional features can collect information about signed-in users when enabled. Site owners should describe their use of analytics in their site’s privacy notice and configure tracking for their visitors as appropriate. Read the Web-Stat privacy policy and service terms.

Support

Need help getting started or reading your reports? Contact Web-Stat support.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, open Plugins > Add New and search for Web-Stat.
  2. Install and activate the plugin. It sets up a Web-Stat account and starts tracking your site.
  3. Open Web-Stat in the WordPress admin menu or click View My Stats to see your visits.
  4. Visit Web-Stat > Settings to adjust tracking or account settings.
sections.faq:
Do I need a separate Web-Stat account?

Yes. Installing the plugin sets up a Web-Stat account for your site. You can open your stats through WordPress or on the Web-Stat website.

Are my analytics stored in my WordPress database?

No. The plugin sends visit data to the Web-Stat hosted service, where your reports are processed. See the privacy links in the description above.

Is the free plan really free?

Yes. The free plan includes up to 5,000 page views per month, the latest 50 visits and one month of report history. You can upgrade if you need more capacity or advanced reports.

Can I see which pages a visitor viewed?

The free plan shows a visitor’s entrance page. Plus adds navigation and click-path reports showing the pages visitors viewed within your site.

Will Web-Stat appear on my site?

Tracking is invisible by default. You can choose to display a visitor counter in Web-Stat > Settings.

How do I change plans or find my login details?

Use Web-Stat > Settings in your WordPress admin area, or open your account on the Web-Stat website. See the plan comparison for feature details.
